premises.name: account03/B12 QFORM-TWO-SAMESIGN-THREEBLOCK-v1
premises.scope: a physical 3x3 block with two same-sign eigenvalues of magnitude >=L and arbitrary third eigenvalue gives full density cap C_*/L; outside coefficients/cross couplings arbitrary

new_results: For A=2 sigma I_4+(tau-2 sigma)vv^T with v=(sqrt(q),sqrt(1-q),0,0), spec(A)={2 sigma,2 sigma,2 sigma,tau} and scalar pivot a=2 sigma(1-q)+tau q has Schur complement diag(2 sigma tau/a,2 sigma,2 sigma).

The complementary physical triple always has two eigenvalues exactly 2 sigma, so the completed partner theorem gives ||p||_infinity<=C_*/2=12.091519144980758... uniformly for every real added eigenvalue tau and both signs sigma.

There is no fixed-pivot Schur stability modulus depending only on the magnitude of the added spectral eigenvalue: a commuting extra eigenvalue tau->0 can produce Schur norm ->infinity through pivot cancellation while the full density remains uniformly bounded.
The same fixed-pivot failure occurs for |tau|->infinity; global sign reflection realizes both signs of added eigenvalue.
Any extra-eigenvalue recurrence must retain the physical pivot-gap denominator or switch to another physical/aggregate certificate before inversion.

stress_families.small_spike: q=1-e, tau=-e(2-e)/(1-e), final pivot=e^2, exceptional Schur eigenvalue=-2(2-e)/(e(1-e)); |tau|<=3e but |Schur|>4/e
stress_families.large_spike: q=e, tau=3-2/e, final pivot=e, exceptional Schur eigenvalue=6/e-4/e^2; for e<=1/3, |tau|>=1/e and |Schur|>=2/e^2

checker.type: exact symbolic SymPy identities for generic Schur law and small/large spike sequences

unresolved_implication: For an arbitrary symmetric matrix with only three globally large eigenvalues, force or aggregate a source-valid certificate switch before a local pivot/minor becomes tiny; no single uniformly good physical block is guaranteed by the live structural corrections.
next_step: Use this Mobius-pole stress family as a mandatory test while attempting an aggregate-before-inversion rule that switches between heavy pivots, two-same-sign physical blocks, and grouped cross-bank certificates.
